Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
value.conclusion: dim_H(E x [0,1]) = dim_H(E) + 1, with the Euclidean metric under Eucl(n) x R = Eucl(n+1), including n=0.

definitions.type: family of Euclidean metric spaces indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: For each natural number m, Eucl(m)=R^m with distance between x and y equal to (sum_{j=1}^m (x_j-y_j)^2)^(1/2). Eucl(0) is the singleton empty tuple. Identify Eucl(m) x R with Eucl(m+1) by concatenating coordinates; its distance is sqrt(dist(x,y)^2+|t-u|^2), throughout, including m=0.

definitions.type: extended nonnegative diameter of a subset of a metric space
definitions.definition: diam(A)=sup{dist(x,y):x,y in A}, with diameter of the empty set zero; it may be infinity. In a native extended metric space the same quantity is ediam(A). At finite diameter it is identified with its nonnegative real value.

definitions.type: unnormalized Hausdorff contents and Hausdorff measures of Euclidean sets
definitions.definition:
For a Euclidean set \(A\), exponent \(s>0\), and scale \(\delta>0\), put

\[
H^s_\delta(A)=\inf\left\{\sum_i(\operatorname{diam}U_i)^s:
 A\subseteq\bigcup_iU_i,\quad\operatorname{diam}U_i\leq\delta\right\},
\qquad H^s(A)=\sup_{\delta>0}H^s_\delta(A).
\]

Covers are countable, with empty members contributing zero.

definitions.type: native Hausdorff measure notation for real exponents on extended metric spaces
definitions.definition: muH[a] denotes Mathlib MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure a, constructed as the metric measure from the set cost ediam(U)^a, using the Borel measurable structure; its construction is native mkMetric (fun r => r^a). This definition asserts no comparison with H. Native infinite sums and integrals take values in [0,infinity].

binders.type: subset of the ambient extended metric space

definitions.type: native Hausdorff dimension of a subset of an extended metric space
definitions.definition: dimH(A) is the native Mathlib Hausdorff dimension: sup over nonnegative real a such that muH[a](A)=infinity of a, as an element of [0,infinity], with supremum of the empty family zero. The measurable structure used here is Borel.

binders.type: subset of an extended metric space

definitions.type: Hausdorff dimension of a Euclidean set
definitions.definition: dim_H(A) is the usual Hausdorff dimension, represented by dimH(A) on its Euclidean metric. Its meaning is the supremum of nonnegative exponents a for which the native Hausdorff measure muH[a](A) is infinite, with supremum of the empty family zero. Values lie in [0,infinity]. Its equivalence with the critical exponent of the supplied unnormalized covering measure is a proof obligation, not an original hypothesis.

definitions.type: Lebesgue measure on the real line and nonnegative Lebesgue integration
definitions.definition: lambda is Lebesgue length measure on R, with its Lebesgue measurable structure. Integrals below are nonnegative Lebesgue integrals valued in [0,infinity]; integration over a measurable set uses the restricted measure. For a set J, 1_J(t) is 1 when t belongs to J and 0 otherwise. The notation |J| means lambda(J).
F=E x I under the Euclidean coordinate concatenation in D001.
D=dim_H(E), initially an extended nonnegative real number; no finiteness property is assumed in this definition.

value.representation_notes: n : ℕ and E : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) preserve every ambient dimension including zero. The actual pinned EuclideanSpace is PiLp 2 (fun _ => ℝ): 2 is the extended-nonnegative Lp exponent, and Fin n is the finite coordinate index, not an order/capability assumption. Its distance is the square root of the sum of squared coordinate distances. WithLp.toLp changes the type synonym and Fin.snoc appends one coordinate; YF uses this concatenation inside Eucl(n+1), never the default sup metric on a product. T003 proves its distance formula, inverses and projection contractions. YLine and T004 check the real-line/Eucl(1) identification already used in the source. Metric.ediam is the ENNReal supremum of pairwise edist, with empty diameter zero. YCover uses arbitrary sequences of subsets, no measurability restriction; finite or other countable covers are represented with empty padding. YCost uses ENNReal real powers; every use has positive exponent, so empty terms vanish. YContent infimizes those costs at positive real scales; YHaus supremizes positive real scales. The equality with native unnormalized hausdorffMeasure is an obligation T001, not a definition. YCritical packages exactly the critical-exponent clauses. dimH is the native ENNReal supremum over nonnegative real exponents with infinite Borel Hausdorff measure, matching D005/D006 including infinity and empty supremum zero. ENNReal.ofReal s identifies a positive real exponent with its extended value; n casts to a finite ENNReal natural. D remains dimH E until T006 proves finiteness; any later toReal requires this fact. Lebesgue integration uses the native real volume and restricted measure; Borel-measurable open intervals give the requisite a.e. measurable nonnegative summands, agreeing with Lebesgue length/integration for these functions. The pinned M001-M006 are used directly as library theorems, not project premises. Background notes remain optional implementation references.

steps.statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (A : Set (YEucl m)) (s : ℝ), 0 < s → YHaus s A = MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure s A
steps.explanation: Unfold the checked hausdorffMeasure_apply formula. Positive real scales cover all finite positive extended scales; the infinity scale contributes no larger infimum. Positive real powers give zero for empty members, so natural-number covers with empty padding implement the source countable covers exactly.

steps.statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (A : Set (YEucl m)), YCritical A
steps.explanation: Export all clauses of N001. Use the pinned four critical-exponent lemmas directly, passing the nonnegative exponent Real.toNNReal s and proving its real/ENNReal coercions equal s/ofReal s from 0<s. dimH has ENNReal codomain and Borel measurable structure. No M premise ports.

steps.statement: (∀ (m : ℕ) (x y : YEucl m) (t u : ℝ), dist (YJoin x t) (YJoin y u) = Real.sqrt (dist x y ^ 2 + |t-u| ^ 2)) ∧ (∀ (m : ℕ) (z : YEucl (m+1)), YJoin (YBase z) (YLast z) = z) ∧ (∀ (m : ℕ) (x : YEucl m) (t : ℝ), YBase (YJoin x t) = x ∧ YLast (YJoin x t) = t) ∧ (∀ m : ℕ, LipschitzWith 1 (@YBase m) ∧ LipschitzWith 1 (@YLast m)) ∧ Isometry YLine ∧ Function.Surjective YLine
steps.explanation: Shared implementation of the actual coordinate identifications in D001. EuclideanSpace.dist_eq/dist_sq_eq compute the sum of squared coordinate distances; Fin.snoc appends the last coordinate. Split the finite sum into castSucc coordinates and last. Derive projection contractions and the one-coordinate line isometry, including m=0. These are obligations, not properties hidden in the definitions.

steps.statement: (∀ (s δ : ℝ), 0 < s → 0 < δ → YContent s δ YI = YContent s δ (YLine '' YI)) ∧ (∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → YHaus s YI = YHaus s (YLine '' YI)) ∧ dimH YI = dimH (YLine '' YI)
steps.explanation: Check the real-line/one-coordinate-vector conversion actually used by S009. Push covers forward and pull them back through the surjective isometry YLine; diameters and costs agree, giving content and measure equality. The same isometry preserves native Hausdorff dimension (direct library isometry transport or its defining critical exponents). This is the only real-line/vector conversion; there is no change of norm.

steps.statement: (∃ L : ℝ, 0 < L ∧ ∀ x ∈ E, ∀ i : Fin n, |x i| ≤ L) ∧ (∀ (s δ : ℝ), 0 < s → 0 < δ → YContent s δ E < ⊤)
steps.explanation: Use compactness for a bounding coordinate box and finite ball covers at each positive scale; enumerate finite covers with empty padding. Contents and finite costs stay in ENNReal, so no toReal of infinity is introduced.

steps.statement: (0 ≤ dimH E ∧ dimH E ≤ (n : ℝ≥0∞) ∧ dimH E < ⊤) ∧ (n = 0 → E = Set.univ ∧ E.Subsingleton ∧ dimH E = 0) ∧ (∀ (s δ : ℝ), 0 < s → 0 < δ → YContent s δ E < ⊤)
steps.explanation: Export N002 in full. For n≥1 subdivide the bounding box into O(h^(-n)) cubes of diameter at most sqrt n*h, so each exponent a>n has zero Hausdorff measure. Apply T002 and let a decrease to n. For n=0 use nonemptiness and the unique empty tuple; singleton covers have zero positive cost. Retain finite contents from T005.

steps.statement: ∀ a : ℝ, 1 < a → YHaus a YI = 0
steps.explanation: Use k equal closed intervals with total a-cost k^(1-a); at each positive scale admissibility holds eventually and costs tend to zero.

steps.statement: ∀ (δ : ℝ), 0 < δ → ∀ U : ℕ → Set ℝ, YCover δ YI U → (1 : ℝ≥0∞) ≤ ∑' i, Metric.ediam (U i)
steps.explanation: Keep only nonempty members (a subtype of naturals), enlarge bounded real sets to open intervals with geometric total error ε. Apply Lebesgue length subadditivity and volume I=1, then remove ε with the original cover fixed. Empty padded terms contribute zero.

steps.statement: (∀ (s δ : ℝ), 0 < s → s < 1 → 0 < δ → ∀ U : ℕ → Set ℝ, YCover δ YI U → (ENNReal.ofReal δ) ^ (s-1) ≤ YCost s U) ∧ (∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → s < 1 → YHaus s YI = ⊤)
steps.explanation: For positive diameters ≤δ use the negative exponent s-1; treat diameter zero separately. Sum and use T008, then infimize over covers. As δ tends to zero the lower bound diverges. Real powers are on ENNReal after ofReal; δ>0 is essential.

steps.statement: dimH YI = 1 ∧ (∀ a : ℝ, 1 < a → YHaus a YI = 0) ∧ (∀ (s δ : ℝ), 0 < s → s < 1 → 0 < δ → ∀ U : ℕ → Set ℝ, YCover δ YI U → (1 : ℝ≥0∞) ≤ ∑' i, Metric.ediam (U i) ∧ (ENNReal.ofReal δ) ^ (s-1) ≤ YCost s U) ∧ (∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → s < 1 → YHaus s YI = ⊤)
steps.explanation: Export every N003 clause. Use T004 to transfer the interval to Eucl(1), apply T002, and transfer dimension back. Upper exponents a>1 and lower 0<s<1 force dimension exactly one by order completeness; retain the coverwise estimates.

steps.statement: n = 0 → dimH (YF E) ≤ dimH E + 1
steps.explanation: Under n=0, N002 identifies E with the singleton and D=0. Send covers of I through t↦YJoin (empty tuple) t, after intersecting members with I. T003 gives the isometry; obtain zero a-measure for a>1, apply T002 and let a decrease to one.

steps.statement: 1 ≤ n → ∀ q : ℝ, 0 < q → dimH E < ENNReal.ofReal q → ∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → r ≤ 1 → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ U : ℕ → Set (YEucl n), YCover r E U ∧ (∀ i, (U i).Nonempty → 0 < Metric.ediam (U i)) ∧ YCost q U < ENNReal.ofReal ε

Retain original indices, discard empty members, and replace nonempty zero-diameter singletons by arbitrarily small positive-radius balls. Because n≥1 these balls have positive diameter; assign geometric q-cost bounds. Empty padding remains legal.

steps.statement: 1 ≤ n → ∀ q : ℝ, 0 < q → dimH E < ENNReal.ofReal q → ∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → r ≤ 1 → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ V : ℕ → Set (YEucl (n+1)), YCover (Real.sqrt 2 * r) (YF E) V ∧ YCost (q+1) V < ENNReal.ofReal (2 * (Real.sqrt 2) ^ (q+1) * ε)
steps.explanation: Take T012's cover, partition I into ceil(1/r_i) intervals for each nonempty member, and enumerate the countable union of finite product families. The coordinate distance identity bounds product diameter by sqrt 2*r_i. Use ceil(1/r_i)≤2/r_i and the source cost estimate; padding empty terms costs zero.

steps.statement: 1 ≤ n → ∀ q : ℝ, dimH E < ENNReal.ofReal q → YHaus (q+1) (YF E) = 0 ∧ dimH (YF E) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (q+1)
steps.explanation: N002 and q>D imply q>0. For each target δ>0 choose r=min(1,δ/sqrt 2) and arbitrary ε>0 in T013. The fixed finite cost multiplier lets content vanish, hence Hausdorff measure vanishes. Apply T002 in ambient dimension n+1.

steps.statement: dimH (YF E) ≤ dimH E + 1
steps.explanation: Export N004. The finite ENNReal dimension D from N002 has a real value only after proving finiteness. Use q>D tending to D to get the bound in the n≥1 branch; combine with T011 in the exhaustive natural-number cases.

steps.statement: ∀ (s δ : ℝ), 0 < s → 0 < δ → ∀ V : ℕ → Set (YEucl (n+1)), YCover δ (YF E) V → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ J : ℕ → Set ℝ, (∀ i, IsOpen (J i)) ∧ (∀ i, YLast '' (V i) ⊆ J i) ∧ (∀ i, MeasureTheory.volume (J i) ≤ Metric.ediam (V i) + ENNReal.ofReal (ε * (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(i : ℤ)-1) / (1 + (Metric.ediam (V i)).toReal ^ s))) ∧ (∀ t ∈ YI, YContent s δ E ≤ ∑' i, (Metric.ediam (V i)) ^ s * (J i).indicator (fun _ : ℝ => (1 : ℝ≥0∞)) t)
steps.explanation: Use the checked coordinate projections. For each nonempty V_i take the open enlargement of its last projection with η_i=ε*2^(-i-1)/(1+rho_i^s), where rho_i=(ediam V_i).toReal is justified by δ-finiteness. For empty V_i use J_i=∅. The projected first coordinates with t∈J_i cover E; their diameter bound gives the pointwise majorant. No measurability of V_i or its projections is required; only J_i is open.

steps.statement: ∀ (s δ : ℝ), 0 < s → 0 < δ → ∀ V : ℕ → Set (YEucl (n+1)), YCover δ (YF E) V → YContent s δ E ≤ YCost (s+1) V
steps.explanation: Integrate T016's pointwise majorant for each ε>0 over MeasureTheory.volume.restrict YI. Openness supplies measurability and hence a.e. measurability of each ENNReal-valued indicator times the finite nonnegative coefficient. Apply the checked MeasureTheory.lintegral_tsum with index ℕ. Volume(YI)=1 and the interval length bounds give c≤cost+ε by the geometric error sum. If cost=∞ finish immediately; otherwise remove ε, keeping V fixed. N002 supplies finite c. All real/ENNReal power and toReal conversions use the cover's finite diameter bound and s>0.

steps.statement: ∀ (s δ : ℝ), 0 < s → 0 < δ → YContent s δ E ≤ YContent (s+1) δ (YF E)
steps.explanation: Export N005: infimize the coverwise inequality over every countable δ-cover V. Same scale, Euclidean metric, all n including zero, and arbitrary covering sets.

steps.statement: 0 < dimH E → dimH E + 1 ≤ dimH (YF E)
steps.explanation: Export N006. For each real 0<s<D, T002 gives infinite s-measure of E; take the supremum in T018 to get infinite (s+1)-measure of F, hence dimension≥s+1. Finiteness and positivity of D justify taking s↑D. The final inequality is in ENNReal, allowing infinite dimension of F.

steps.statement: dimH E = 0 → (1 : ℝ≥0∞) ≤ dimH (YF E) ∧ (1 : ℝ≥0∞) = dimH E + 1
steps.explanation: Export N007. Select x0∈E using H001. T003 proves t↦YJoin x0 t is isometric. Pull arbitrary covers of F back to I to compare contents and their suprema. N003 gives infinite s-measure for 0<s<1, so T002 gives dimH F≥s. Let s↑1 and substitute D=0; the proof includes n=0.

steps.statement: dimH (YF E) = dimH E + 1
steps.explanation: Export the full target P. N002 gives the exhaustive D>0 or D=0 cases; use their lower bounds and N004's upper bound, then antisymmetry. YF is exactly the coordinate-concatenated E×[0,1].

1: # Hausdorff dimension of a product with an interval
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: Elias M. Stein and Rami Shakarchi, *Real Analysis: Measure Theory,
6: Integration, and Hilbert Spaces*, Princeton Lectures in Analysis III,
7: Chapter 7, Problems, exercise 9, printed page 388.
8: Book DOI: [10.1515/9781400835560](https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400835560).
9: 
10: > 9. Let \(E\) be a compact set in \(\mathbb R^{d-1}\). Show that
11: > \(\dim(E\times I)=\dim(E)+1\), where \(I\) is the unit interval in
12: > \(\mathbb R\).
13: 
14: ## Fixed interpretation and complete target
15: 
16: Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
17: 2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
18: \(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
19: the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.
20: 
21: Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
22: compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
23: with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove
24: 
25: \[
26: \dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
27: \]
28: 
29: The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
30: formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
31: 
32: ## Fixed natural-language proof
33: 
34: For a Euclidean set \(A\), exponent \(s>0\), and scale \(\delta>0\), put
35: 
36: \[
37: H^s_\delta(A)=\inf\left\{\sum_i(\operatorname{diam}U_i)^s:
38:  A\subseteq\bigcup_iU_i,\quad\operatorname{diam}U_i\leq\delta\right\},
39: \qquad H^s(A)=\sup_{\delta>0}H^s_\delta(A).
40: \]
41: 
42: Covers are countable, with empty members contributing zero. This
43: unnormalized Hausdorff measure gives the usual Hausdorff dimension. We use
44: its critical-exponent characterization: \(H^s(A)=0\) if
45: \(s>\dim_H A\), and \(H^s(A)=\infty\) if \(0<s<\dim_H A\).
46: Conversely, zero measure implies \(\dim_H A\leq s\), and infinite
47: measure implies \(\dim_H A\geq s\).
48: 
49: Write \(D=\dim_H E\) and \(F=E\times[0,1]\). First \(0\leq D\leq n\).
50: Indeed, compactness makes \(E\) bounded. When \(n>0\), a box containing
51: it admits a cover by at most \(Ch^{-n}\) cubes of side at most \(h\),
52: for \(0<h\leq1\). Here \(C\) depends only on that box. Each cube has
53: diameter at most \(\sqrt n h\). For any \(s>n\), the total \(s\)-cost
54: is at most \(C n^{s/2}h^{s-n}\to0\). These arbitrarily fine covers
55: give \(H^s(E)=0\) and hence \(D\leq n\). If \(n=0\), nonemptiness
56: makes \(E=\mathbb R^0\), a singleton of zero \(s\)-cost for every
57: \(s>0\); thus \(D=0\).
58: 
59: ### Upper bound
60: 
61: When \(n=0\), \(F\) is isometric to \([0,1]\). Dividing this interval
62: into \(N\) equal pieces gives total \(a\)-cost \(N^{1-a}\to0\) for
63: every \(a>1\), proving \(\dim_H F\leq1=D+1\).
64: For this upper-bound argument now assume \(n\geq1\).
65: 
66: Fix \(q>D\). Since \(q>0\) and \(H^q(E)=0\), for every
67: \(0<r\leq1\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) there is a countable cover
68: \((U_i)\) of \(E\) with nonempty-member diameters
69: \(0<r_i\leq r\) and \(\sum_i r_i^q<\varepsilon\).
70: The positive-diameter requirement costs nothing: start with a cover of
71: cost below \(\varepsilon/2\); replace each zero-diameter singleton by
72: a ball of diameter at most \(r\), choosing the \(i\)-th replacement
73: to have \(q\)-cost less than \(\varepsilon2^{-i-2}\). The added cost
74: is less than \(\varepsilon/2\). Discard empty members.
75: 
76: Let \(N_i=\lceil1/r_i\rceil\). Partition \([0,1]\) into \(N_i\)
77: closed intervals of length \(1/N_i\leq r_i\). Because \(r_i\leq1\),
78: \(N_i\leq2/r_i\). The corresponding products with \(U_i\) form a
79: countable cover of \(F\). Each has Euclidean diameter at most
80: \(\sqrt2 r_i\), and their total \((q+1)\)-cost is at most
81: 
82: \[
83: \sum_iN_i(\sqrt2 r_i)^{q+1}
84: \leq2(\sqrt2)^{q+1}\sum_i r_i^q
85: <2(\sqrt2)^{q+1}\varepsilon.
86: \]
87: 
88: For any target scale \(\delta>0\), choose
89: \(r\leq\min(1,\delta/\sqrt2)\), then let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
90: Thus \(H^{q+1}_\delta(F)=0\) for every scale, so
91: \(H^{q+1}(F)=0\) and \(\dim_H F\leq q+1\). Letting \(q\downarrow D\)
92: gives \(\dim_H F\leq D+1\).
93: 
94: ### Lower bound when \(D>0\)
95: 
96: Fix \(0<s<D\). Then \(H^s(E)=\infty\), so
97: \(H^s_\delta(E)\) becomes arbitrarily large as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
98: We claim that, for every \(\delta>0\),
99: 
100: \[
101: H^s_\delta(E)\leq H^{s+1}_\delta(F).                 \tag{1}
102: \]
103: 
104: Take an arbitrary countable \(\delta\)-cover \((V_i)_{i\geq0}\) of
105: \(F\), discarding empty members. Define
106: \(\rho_i=\operatorname{diam}V_i\),
107: \(A_i=\pi_{\mathbb R^n}(V_i)\), and
108: \(B_i=\pi_{\mathbb R}(V_i)\). Coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz,
109: so both projected diameters are at most \(\rho_i\leq\delta\).
110: For \(\varepsilon>0\), put
111: 
112: \[
113: \eta_i=\frac{\varepsilon2^{-i-1}}{1+\rho_i^s}>0.
114: \]
115: 
116: Enclose \(B_i\) in an open interval \(J_i\) of length at most
117: \(\rho_i+\eta_i\): its supremum minus infimum is at most \(\rho_i\),
118: and an enlargement of total width \(\eta_i\) suffices. This avoids
119: assuming that the arbitrary covering sets or their projections are measurable.
120: 
121: For each \(t\in[0,1]\), the sets \(A_i\) for which \(t\in J_i\)
122: cover \(E\). Indeed, a point \((x,t)\in F\) belongs to some \(V_i\),
123: giving \(x\in A_i\) and \(t\in B_i\subset J_i\). Their diameters
124: are at most \(\rho_i\). Consequently, with \(c=H^s_\delta(E)\),
125: 
126: \[
127: c\leq\sum_i\rho_i^s\mathbf1_{J_i}(t)\quad(t\in[0,1]).
128: \]
129: 
130: The constant \(c\) is finite: compactness gives a finite cover of \(E\)
131: by balls of diameter at most \(\delta\), with finite \(s\)-cost.
132: Each summand is nonnegative and measurable since \(J_i\) is open.
133: Integrate over \([0,1]\), of Lebesgue measure one, and use Tonelli's
134: theorem for this nonnegative series. Since
135: \(|J_i\cap[0,1]|\leq\rho_i+\eta_i\),
136: 
137: \[
138: \begin{aligned}
139: c&\leq\sum_i\rho_i^s|J_i\cap[0,1]|\\
140:  &\leq\sum_i\rho_i^{s+1}+\sum_i\eta_i\rho_i^s
141:  \leq\sum_i\rho_i^{s+1}+\varepsilon.
142: \end{aligned}
143: \]
144:

22:    hash-bound receipt passes. Repair located failures with the interface author
23:    and have the same separate reviewer assess changed output. Final machine Audit B
24:    inherits that review only if the actual complete artifact preserves the freeze. The
25:    lower-level legacy mechanical freeze can record `PENDING_AUDIT_B`; it does
26:    not satisfy this normal-workflow pre-proof gate.
27: 4. Run local proof workers on frozen conditional obligations. Each gets its
28:    input statements, matched source paragraphs and own compact note index.
29:    Read a full note only if useful. No sibling proof bodies, other cases,
30:    developer history or additional personal skills are supplied.
31:    Use [Lean implementation safeguards](lean-writing.md) for library
32:    applications and conversions, including small type checks in preparation.
33:    Yui proof workers receive these requirements in their stage instructions.
34: 5. Attempt mechanical [assembly](assembly.md) and complete native inspection.
35:    Use the serial connection author only for real connection/library-discharge
36:    repair under unchanged E/P/definitions. Normal final Audit B is machine-only:
37:    inherit the actual pre-proof semantics after checking full endpoint types,
38:    defining header and complete closure. Only proof-valid interface drift opens
39:    B-final. Faithful drift is warning-qualified; a nonpass waits for the user's
40:    explicit delivery/recheck/translation-reset choice. Invalid proof is never
41:    semantically overridden.
42: 
43: ## Background notes are references, not extra ports
44: 
45: New contracts select `source.background_mode: node_local_reference`. Original
46: H/E/M/N/P entries remain unchanged; Audit A's verified supplement remains
47: hash-bound. Do not turn every note into a new M root, retype its entire library
48: signature, or require an extra theorem merely to restate it. The frozen
49: stage-one text's historical `background.effective` expansion is still supported
50: as `promoted_inputs` for old contracts; it is not the new translation default.
51: 
52: At the pre-freeze semantic review and final Audit B, notes are guidance, not library permissions. All proved results in
53: the pinned Mathlib environment are available without registration. Review every
54: external E and complete P against its actual Lean type using the concise author
55: correspondence explanation; independently check direct or equivalent meaning.
56: A new external assumption or stronger hypothesis still returns to the source
57: boundary. See [the complete Audit B standard](audit-b.md).
58: 
59: ## Work continuously, report genuine blockers
60: 
61: There is no ordinary `TASK_INCOMPLETE` reporting tool. While unfinished, keep
62: making concrete edits, queries or proof checks. Submit a completed artifact or
63: report a supported mathematical/source/input blocker. If a model turn ends
64: without either, the controller sends one short continuation instruction; it
65: does not demand a progress essay. State/usage recording is programmatic.
66: Proof workers follow [structured diagnosis and repair](proof-repair.md): report
67: actual packet obstructions. Progress counters are passive; no idle-turn count
68: cancels sibling work or authorizes interface changes.
69: 
70: Whole-case/stage execution, total tokens and calls are unlimited by default.
71: Each native check has the configured 300-second wall limit and finite Lean
72: heartbeat policy. Keep measuring usage and allow explicit
73: cancellation. Only a user-requested finite case deadline covers the entire
74: translation, including preparation, queue waiting, parallel proofs, assembly
75: and Audit B; later stages cannot reset that optional deadline. Preserve partial
76: results and report execution health separately from mathematical acceptance.

import Mathlib
open scoped ENNReal NNReal
noncomputable section
abbrev YEucl (m : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)
def YI : Set ℝ := Set.Icc 0 1
def YJoin {m : ℕ} (x : YEucl m) (t : ℝ) : YEucl (m + 1) :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.snoc (fun i => x i) t)
def YBase {m : ℕ} (z : YEucl (m + 1)) : YEucl m :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => z i.castSucc)
def YLast {m : ℕ} (z : YEucl (m + 1)) : ℝ := z (Fin.last m)
def YF {m : ℕ} (A : Set (YEucl m)) : Set (YEucl (m + 1)) :=
  {z | ∃ x ∈ A, ∃ t ∈ YI, z = YJoin x t}
def YLine (t : ℝ) : YEucl 1 := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun _ => t)
def YCover {X : Type*} [PseudoEMetricSpace X]
    (δ : ℝ) (A : Set X) (U : ℕ → Set X) : Prop :=
  A ⊆ ⋃ i, U i ∧ ∀ i, Metric.ediam (U i) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal δ
def YCost {X : Type*} [PseudoEMetricSpace X]
    (s : ℝ) (U : ℕ → Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ∑' i, (Metric.ediam (U i)) ^ s
def YContent {X : Type*} [PseudoEMetricSpace X]
    (s δ : ℝ) (A : Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (U : ℕ → Set X) (_ : YCover δ A U), YCost s U
def YHaus {X : Type*} [PseudoEMetricSpace X]
    (s : ℝ) (A : Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨆ (δ : ℝ) (_ : 0 < δ), YContent s δ A
def YCritical {X : Type*} [EMetricSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X]
    (A : Set X) : Prop :=
  0 ≤ dimH A ∧ ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s →
    YHaus s A = MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure s A ∧
    (dimH A < ENNReal.ofReal s → YHaus s A = 0) ∧
    (ENNReal.ofReal s < dimH A → YHaus s A = ⊤) ∧
    (YHaus s A = 0 → dimH A ≤ ENNReal.ofReal s) ∧
    (YHaus s A = ⊤ → ENNReal.ofReal s ≤ dimH A)

1: # Audit B: endpoint fidelity and checked Lean closure
2: 
3: The stage-two policy is `endpoint-fidelity-2` (Audit B schema version 2).
4: Its semantic objects are every original external theorem E and the complete
5: final target P. P includes its parameters, quantifiers, hypotheses, domains and
6: conclusion. Accepted NL0/Audit A remains the source authority; B does not repeat
7: unchanged natural-language proof checking.
8: 
9: ## Normal final acceptance and deviation exception
10: 
11: The normal workflow uses `yui-frozen-interface-acceptance-1`. A complete independent
12: pre-proof review establishes source-to-type fidelity for every E and full P and
13: all definitions needed to interpret them. Final native inspection compares the
14: actual exported full types against that frozen contract, checks the exact defining
15: header/pins and semantic receipt, and validates standalone proof/dependency/trust
16: closure. This normal final gate is pure machine work: no additional final LLM is
17: called. It records inherited semantics, not a newly performed independent Audit B.
18: 
19: The actual E/P types include retained hypotheses and quantifiers. Text labels or
20: a source-hash check alone do not establish this gate. The original mathematical
21: review may be wrong; the machine establishes preservation of that reviewed encoding,
22: not correctness of the reviewer's natural-language judgment.
23: 
24: Only complete proof-integrity success plus genuine endpoint/definition drift may
25: open the exceptional independent B-final review below. A faithful result then has
26: `AUDIT-B-CONDITIONAL`, a freeze-deviation warning and an explicit harness-defect
27: report. Invalid native evidence, incomplete dependencies or changed provenance
28: cannot be overridden semantically. Nonfaithful/unverified results wait for the
29: three explicit user choices in [proof repair](proof-repair.md); accepting a different
30: result does not complete the original target. Explicit/manual legacy semantic
31: receipts remain supported under their original schemas and are not relabeled.
32: Explicitly nonindependent/self-review records remain readable development checks;
33: they cannot grant whole-workflow Audit B acceptance. The same qualification rule
34: applies to supplied Audit A authority and incremental producer/cut reviews.
35: 
36: ## Author correspondence explanations
37: 
38: During interface authoring, provide `endpoint_correspondence`, keyed by every
39: E ID and P. Each entry is `{mode: direct|equivalent, explanation: string}`.
40: Keep it short and useful; do not restate the entire proof or manufacture a
41: line-by-line formalization commentary:
42: 
43: - **Direct:** identify the corresponding variables, hypotheses and assertion.
44:   One sentence is enough when the translation is immediate.
45: - **Equivalent:** explain the mathematical identification or reformulation,
46:   why it works in both directions and which existing conditions it uses.
47:   Point to relevant definitions or checked conversions when needed.
48: 
49: For example, expressing invariance under a finite basis of operators can encode
50: invariance under their linear span: explain the spanning property and closure
51: of a subspace under linear combinations. The review must establish those facts
52: for the actual source algebra/action; the word “equivalent” alone is insufficient.
53: 
54: The postprocessing author carries these notes into each E/P entry in
55: `mapping.json`, checks them against the actual export and completes missing
56: notes for older frozen contracts. It must not change frozen proof statements
57: or bodies merely to improve a note. An explanation is an author's claim, not
58: an Audit B verdict or a formal proof.
59: 
60: ## Semantic responsibility before freeze or at explicit B-final
61: 
62: Read the explanation together with the original source statement and actual
63: elaborated Lean type. Follow the definitions needed to interpret the endpoint,
64: including structure fields that might hide extra assumptions. Check each E/P
65: row, then these four global checks:
66: 
67: 1. `endpoint_inventory_and_scope`: all original E statements and P are covered;
68:    the source version, reviewer scope and inherited qualifications are explicit.
69: 2. `external_statement_fidelity`: each external assumption has the source's
70:    complete mathematical meaning, including conditions and quantifiers. With
71:    no external inputs, record that fact.
72: 3. `complete_target_and_representations`: the entire target theorem has the
73:    same meaning, including every hypothesis. Validate the explanation of each
74:    direct or equivalent encoding and relevant edge cases.
75: 4. `kernel_closure_and_trust`: the actual exported proof compiled, all required
76:    producers and intermediate library ports were discharged, and the checked
77:    root has only the declared external assumptions and permitted foundations.
78: 
79: Equivalent formulations are allowed. Do not reject a faithful encoding because
80: it lacks a particular Mathlib type/name, a separate object for every NL0
81: D node, or a duplicate formal representation. A mathematical source-to-code
82: identification can be checked semantically without constructing an unnecessary
83: second model. If the implementation actually crosses two different Lean
84: representations, the required conversion must occur in checked Lean code.
85: Unexplained equivalence, stronger assumptions, missing hypotheses, changed
86: domains or hidden target assumptions remain defects.
87: 
88: Do not accept an explanation on trust or copy the author's conclusion into the
89: review. Record PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED with specific findings and source/type/note
90: locations. A compiler pass cannot substitute for this independent judgment.
91: 
92: ## Freely available Mathlib
93: 
94: All proved results in the pinned Mathlib environment are available in stage
95: two. Do not compare their names, counts or node-by-node uses with the NL0 M
96: inventory. There is no per-M semantic row, imported-proof whitelist,
97: `calculation_links` ledger, or separate review of implementation N/D nodes.
98: Definitions are examined when they determine endpoint meaning, not for an
99: exact inventory match. Notes from Audit A are optional local guidance, not
100: permissions to use a library theorem.
101: 
102: New interfaces normally use Mathlib directly. An older or deliberately
103: conditional interface can retain M ports; `library_terms` supplies an actual
104: Lean proof for each such port at assembly. These are discharge proofs, not a
105: library correspondence inventory. They cannot remain unproved assumptions of
106: the final export. New external axioms or stronger project hypotheses still
107: require returning to the affected source boundary.
108: 
109: ## Mechanical evidence and limits
110: 
111: ### Compact review materials
112: 
113: The semantic reviewer reads the separately versioned
114: `yui-audit-b-review-view-1` in `review-packet.json`. Start at `/scope` and
115: `/mechanical_summary`, then examine each `/endpoints/<ID>` source, actual
116: inspected type and author correspondence. P retains the complete original
117: target, parameters and hypotheses. The view is a deterministic Python extraction,
118: not an LLM summary or mathematical judgment. It never substitutes a declared
119: expected type for the actual inspected type.
120: 
121: `/documents` identifies hash-bound `source-context.json`, `source-original.txt`
122: and actual `Proof.lean`. Read relevant original and Lean definitions there,
123: including hidden structure fields, when needed to interpret an endpoint.
124: Complete raw compiler, elaboration and dependency records stay in the machine
125: archive; they are not default reviewer inputs. A mechanical summary reports
126: actual checks and exceptions, without populating a semantic PASS. The full
127: dependency inspection remains a program responsibility.
128: 
129: Use `read_task_input` JSON pointers, not guessed fixed line positions. Large
130: containers expose keys and large strings expose `next_offset`. Text reads
131: resume with `next_start` and `next_column`. Serialized read results are at most
132: 32 KiB; follow `has_more` until the needed statement is complete. This pagination
133: limit is not a task time/token/call budget. Unknown calls or modified feedback
134: remain rejected with a specific local protocol fault, not a retryable HTTP 502.
135: 
136: ### Explicit reuse of completed native evidence
137: 
138: `audit_b.py reuse-review <new-directory> --original <old-audit-directory>`
139: prepares a new semantic review without rebuilding or changing Lean. It validates
140: every original input and snapshot, the original native artifacts/output, source
141: and accepted-A authority, environment pins, and the exact historical tool
142: snapshots. The new view and current reviewer runtime are separately bound in
143: `review-reuse.json`; the normal current-build tool check is not disabled.
144: Changed or incomplete evidence blocks reuse. Preserve the original failure.
145: 
146: The new independent reviewer receives no previous B verdict, reviewer history,
147: owner reasoning or other-case material. The receipt discloses inherited native
148: checks and a new semantic review; it cannot claim fresh compilation, an unaided
149: cold whole-workflow success or measured acceleration. Changing proofs or source
150: requires the appropriate new checks, rather than this review-only path.
151: 
152: `audit_b.py prepare/build/check` binds the source, accepted A, contract, plan,
153: proofs, tool versions and environment hashes. Build compiles standalone
154: `Proof.lean` before adding inspection. It checks E/P against their declared
155: encoded types, modulo definitional equality and bijective universe renaming.
156: It does not prove equivalence between natural-language text and Lean.
157: Distinct universes must not be collapsed; changed types or hypotheses must not
158: be normalized away. Source fidelity is established by the bound pre-proof independent review, or an actual exceptional B-final review; this native comparison does not establish it anew.
159: 
160: Inspection follows the actual `AuditBExport.P` closure. No `sorry`, unproved
161: local axiom/opaque substitute or undeclared foundation may be introduced.
162: Local bodies still compile against their own task inputs and the pinned
163: library; every required producer must exist. Assembly, inspection and semantic
164: review have separate recorded outcomes.
165: 
166: Version-1 receipts remain historical results under their original policy.
167: They cannot be silently relabeled or accepted as version-2 reviews. Start a
168: new bound audit when policy, source, code or evidence changes. Pending templates
169: never pass. A whole accepted source plus complete native gates and its bound semantic
170: authority yields `AUDIT-B-PASSED`; a fragment yields at most the explicitly
171: scoped development verdict. A whole source with an actual conditional Audit A
172: can yield `AUDIT-B-CONDITIONAL` after all the same native and semantic checks.
173: It retains the exact source warnings and never upgrades them to full PASS.
174: Neither proves external publications in Lean or
175: establishes formalizer speedup. Preserve failures and report actual costs.

1: # Lean implementation safeguards
2: 
3: Apply these requirements within the accepted NL0 and the fixed Lean interface.
4: They govern implementation, not additional NL0 detail or a weaker Audit B.
5: Use existing library readers and local checking tools; no separate review
6: model, new premise or mandatory lookup of every familiar declaration is needed.
7: 
8: 1. **Check critical library signatures.** Before relying on a critical or
9:    unfamiliar library application, establish its complete type in the pinned
10:    environment, including explicit, implicit and instance binders and all
11:    side conditions. Read the declaration or check a small typed application
12:    when its signature is uncertain. Do not infer the calling convention from
13:    its name or pass an implicit argument as though it were an explicit one.
14:    A previously checked signature in this context need not be looked up again.
15: 2. **Constrain difficult inference.** When coercions or implicit inference
16:    obscure the intended application, give the intermediate fact an explicit
17:    type and supply the relevant named parameters, such as the set, exponent
18:    or ambient space. Prefer this to leaving Lean to discover those choices by
19:    unfolding large definitions. Routine unambiguous arguments can stay
20:    implicit; explicit parameters must preserve the existing target and inputs.
21: 3. **Check conversions before combining them.** When an argument crosses Lean
22:    representations, first establish a small typed conversion fact, then use
23:    it in the main proof. In particular, distinguish `ℝ`, `ℝ≥0` and `ℝ≥0∞`;
24:    check the conversion direction, nonnegativity and any finiteness conditions.
25:    A conversion is not automatically invertible, and matching notation does
26:    not establish equality of differently typed expressions. Reuse a checked
27:    fact when available. Do not invent another representation, a global helper
28:    requirement or an extra hypothesis just to satisfy this instruction.
29: 4. **Isolate an inference failure.** If compiler feedback identifies a library
30:    application, coercion or expensive inference problem, reduce the next check
31:    to that application or conversion with explicit local types before adding
32:    more proof code. Use `check_auxiliary` in a proof worker, or
33:    `check_lean_types` during preparation when that tool is supplied. Helpers
34:    use only the current allowed inputs and never become new premises. Once
35:    the small check succeeds, integrate the result and recheck the complete
36:    obligation; success of a helper alone does not accept the target.
37: 
38: 5. **Repair after a bounded check.** Native checks have a separate per-call wall
39:    limit, normally 300 seconds, and use Lean's finite default heartbeat budget.
40:    A timeout or heartbeat diagnostic leaves the goal unaccepted and returns
41:    control to the same worker. Inspect the retained candidate and diagnostic,
42:    then check a smaller typed application, conversion or proof fragment before
43:    integrating it. Do not repeat the unchanged expensive candidate or disable
44:    limits to avoid diagnosis. Preserve the target, allowed inputs and proof
45:    requirements; a timeout alone establishes no mathematical gap.

value.text: Fix m,A and s>0 (L1). Apply M002 to Eucl(m), with its Euclidean extended metric and Borel measurable structure, exponent s and set A. At each finite positive scale its inner infimum is exactly H^s_delta(A): every countable cover is enumerable by naturals, with empty padding if needed, and each nonempty-member inner supremum is just its diameter to power s, whereas an empty member has cost zero. At a finite scale all nonempty admissible diameters are finite, so ediam and the usual diameter agree. The additional native scale infinity does not change the outer supremum: its admissible covers include those at every finite scale, so its infimum is no larger. Every positive finite extended scale is a positive real scale. Thus M002 gives muH[s](A)=sup_delta H^s_delta(A)=H^s(A).

Use F001. The native dimension dimH(A) is dim_H(A) by the representation in D006 and is nonnegative because it is a supremum in [0,infinity]. Regard s as a nonnegative real, using s>0. M003 gives infinity when s<dim_H(A); M004 gives zero when dim_H(A)<s. If H^s(A)=0, F001 makes the native measure zero and hence unequal to infinity, so M005 gives dim_H(A)<=s. If H^s(A)=infinity, F001 and M006 give s<=dim_H(A). These conclusions hold for the arbitrary Euclidean dimension m and set A, including infinite dimension values. Discharge L1 and universally quantify: all the asserted clauses follow.

H002 gives compactness. The open balls of radius delta/2 centered at points of E form an open cover; a finite subcover has diameters at most delta and finite s-cost. Thus H^s_delta(E) is finite for arbitrary s>0,delta>0. Also the increasing boxes (-k,k)^n, for positive integer k, cover Eucl(n). A finite subcover of E places E in some [-L,L]^n with L>0. This proves the required existence of a bounding box. Nonnegativity of D follows from N001.

For the branch L1: n>=1, choose the bounding box from F001. Subdivide each coordinate interval [-L,L] into ceil(2L/h) pieces of length at most h, where 0<h<=1. Taking products covers the box by at most (2L/h+1)^n <= C h^(-n) cubes, where C=(2L+2)^n. Each cube has Euclidean diameter at most sqrt(n) h. Hence for any a>n the total a-cost is at most C n^(a/2) h^(a-n), tending to zero as h decreases to zero; the maximum diameter tends to zero as well. For each fixed positive scale these covers eventually satisfy its diameter bound and have arbitrarily small cost. Thus H^a(E)=0. N001 gives D<=a for all a>n, hence D<=n (otherwise choose a strictly between n and D; if D=infinity any a>n contradicts D<=a). Discharge L1 to obtain the conditional branch conclusion.

For the branch L2: n=0, H001 and the fact that Eucl(0) has just its empty tuple give E=Eucl(0), a singleton. For every positive exponent its one-member singleton cover has diameter and cost zero at every scale. N001 therefore gives D is at most every positive real exponent; together with nonnegativity this is D=0. Discharge L2. Since a natural n is either zero or at least one, F003 and this branch yield 0<=D<=n, with the stated singleton assertion when n=0. F002 supplies the finite-content clause.

For any a>1 and each positive integer k, the k closed intervals [j/k,(j+1)/k], 0<=j<k, cover I. Their diameters are 1/k, and their total a-cost is k*(1/k)^a=k^(1-a), tending to zero as k tends to infinity. At any fixed scale the diameter bound holds for all sufficiently large k. Hence the a-content of I is zero at every positive scale and H^a(I)=0 for every a>1.

Fix delta>0 and an arbitrary countable delta-cover T of I. Ignore empty terms by K={i:T_i nonempty}, and set rho_i=diam(T_i)<=delta. For epsilon>0 the bounded nonempty real set T_i has infimum and supremum, with sup T_i-inf T_i=rho_i. Define the open interval J_i=(inf T_i-epsilon*2^(-i-2),sup T_i+epsilon*2^(-i-2)); it contains T_i and has length rho_i+epsilon*2^(-i-1). These intervals cover I. Countable subadditivity of Lebesgue length, lambda(I)=1, and the geometric sum over K bounded by the full sum over N give 1<=sum_i lambda(J_i)<=sum_i rho_i+epsilon. If sum_i rho_i is infinite the claim is immediate; otherwise letting epsilon decrease to zero gives sum_i rho_i>=1. This holds for the arbitrary cover and scale.

For arbitrary 0<s<1, retain delta and T, K, rho. For 0<rho_i<=delta the negative exponent s-1 gives rho_i^(s-1)>=delta^(s-1), hence rho_i^s>=delta^(s-1)*rho_i. When rho_i=0 the same inequality is 0>=0, since s>0. Sum the inequalities and apply F002: sum_i rho_i^s>=delta^(s-1)*sum_i rho_i>=delta^(s-1). The same holds with empty terms contributing zero. Take the infimum over the arbitrary delta-covers to obtain H^s_delta(I)>=delta^(s-1). Since s-1<0 this lower bound tends to infinity as delta decreases to zero; consequently H^s(I)=infinity for every 0<s<1. This also records the coverwise bound required in the output.

Apply N001 with m=1 on the real Euclidean line: identify a real number with its one-coordinate vector in Eucl(1), preserving distance by the Euclidean formula. F001 gives dim_H(I)<=a for every a>1, hence dim_H(I)<=1. F003 gives dim_H(I)>=s for every 0<s<1, hence dim_H(I)>=1 by real order completeness. Together these yield dim_H(I)=1, and F001,F002,F003 retain all of the additional estimates asserted in the output.

First treat L1: n=0. N002 gives E=Eucl(0), a singleton, and D=0. The map from I to F sending t to the concatenated point ((),t) is onto and preserves all distances by the Euclidean formula. N003 gives H^a(I)=0 for every a>1. For any positive scale and cost tolerance, choose a cover of I at that scale with cost below the tolerance, intersect each cover member with I, and send it through this map. These sets cover F and have no larger diameters or costs. Thus H^a(F)=0 for every a>1. By N001, dim_H(F)<=a for every a>1, hence dim_H(F)<=1=D+1. Discharge L1 and retain this branch conclusion.

Assume L2: n>=1. Fix q>D. N002 implies q>0, and N001 gives H^q(E)=0. Thus for any 0<r<=1 and epsilon>0 the infimum H^q_r(E)=0 supplies a countable r-cover with cost below epsilon/2. Discard its empty members. Each remaining zero-diameter set is a singleton. Enumerate such members by their original natural indices i and replace the i-th by a ball centered at that singleton, of positive diameter at most r and with q-cost <epsilon*2^(-i-2). Such balls exist in Eucl(n) because n>=1: their diameters are twice their positive radii, which may be made arbitrarily small since q>0. The replacement costs sum to at most epsilon/2 (indeed the strict bounds have that geometric majorant); with the initial strict epsilon/2 bound the final cost is <epsilon. Unchanged positive-diameter members already have diameter <=r. This proves existence of the positive-diameter cover needed next.

Choose U as in F002 and put r_i=diam(U_i), N_i=ceil(1/r_i). The N_i intervals [j/N_i,(j+1)/N_i], 0<=j<N_i, cover I and have length 1/N_i<=r_i. Since r_i<=1, N_i<=1/r_i+1<=2/r_i. The products of U_i with these intervals form a countable cover of F: a countable union of finite families is countable. By the Euclidean product distance, each product diameter is at most sqrt(2)*r_i. Thus their total (q+1)-cost is at most sum_i N_i*(sqrt(2)*r_i)^(q+1) <= 2*(sqrt(2))^(q+1)*sum_i r_i^q < 2*(sqrt(2))^(q+1)*epsilon. Since r and epsilon were arbitrary and the remaining branch assumption concerns only n, universally quantify them in this cover-existence conclusion.

For an arbitrary target scale delta>0, apply the universally quantified construction F003 with its scale parameter equal to min(1,delta/sqrt(2)), which is strictly positive, and with arbitrary positive cost parameter. The resulting covers are delta-covers of F. Let that cost parameter decrease to zero; the multiplier 2*(sqrt(2))^(q+1) is fixed and finite, so H^(q+1)_delta(F)=0. The scale delta was arbitrary, hence H^(q+1)(F)=0. By N001, dim_H(F)<=q+1. Since q>D was arbitrary, universally quantify q in this conclusion.

N002 makes D finite. Since q>D was arbitrary, F004 holds for every such q. Let q decrease to D (equivalently use q=D+1/k for positive integers k); this gives dim_H(F)<=D+1. Discharge L2. Together with F001 and the exhaustive alternatives n=0 or n>=1, this proves the upper bound.

Fix s>0 and delta>0 and put c=H^s_delta(E). N002 proves c finite. Take an arbitrary countable delta-cover V of F, and restrict to its nonempty-member indices K, a subset of N. Put rho_i=diam(V_i), A_i=the first-coordinate projection of V_i, and B_i=the last-coordinate projection. By the Euclidean distance formula each coordinate projection is 1-Lipschitz: dist of projected points is no more than dist of the original points. Consequently diam(A_i)<=rho_i and diam(B_i)<=rho_i<=delta. Every B_i is nonempty and bounded; its infimum and supremum are finite and sup B_i-inf B_i<=rho_i. No measurability of V_i,A_i or B_i is asserted or needed.

For epsilon>0 define eta_i=epsilon*2^(-i-1)/(1+rho_i^s)>0 and J_i=(inf B_i-eta_i/2,sup B_i+eta_i/2). F001 makes these finite open intervals containing B_i, with length at most rho_i+eta_i. Define f_i(t)=rho_i^s*1_{J_i}(t). Each coefficient is finite and nonnegative, each J_i is open, and therefore every f_i is Lebesgue measurable, hence almost everywhere measurable for lambda restricted to I. The family has countable index set K.

For each t in I the A_i with t in J_i cover E: given x in E, the point (x,t) belongs to F and hence to some V_i. That index lies in K, x belongs to A_i, and t belongs to B_i subset J_i by F002. These A_i have diameter <=rho_i<=delta by F001, so they are an admissible countable delta-cover of E. Its s-cost is at most sum_i rho_i^s*1_{J_i}(t)=sum_i f_i(t). The definition of c as an infimum gives c<=sum_i f_i(t) for every t in I.

Integrate F003 against lambda restricted to I. Since lambda(I)=1, the integral of the finite constant c is c. Apply M001 with X=R, K the countable subset of N above, mu=lambda restricted to I, and the nonnegative measurable family f from F002. It gives integral_I sum_i f_i = sum_i integral_I f_i. For each i, integration of its indicator times the constant gives integral_I f_i=rho_i^s*lambda(J_i intersect I). Thus, using F002,
c <= sum_i rho_i^s*lambda(J_i intersect I) <= sum_i rho_i^s*(rho_i+eta_i) = sum_i rho_i^(s+1)+sum_i eta_i*rho_i^s <= sum_i rho_i^(s+1)+epsilon.
The last bound follows termwise from eta_i*rho_i^s=epsilon*2^(-i-1)*rho_i^s/(1+rho_i^s)<=epsilon*2^(-i-1) and sum_{i in K}2^(-i-1)<=1. All inequalities are valid for nonnegative extended sums. If the cost sum_i rho_i^(s+1) is infinite, c<=that cost immediately. Otherwise the cost and c are finite, and since this estimate is available for every epsilon>0, let epsilon decrease to zero to obtain c<=sum_i rho_i^(s+1). The interval enlargement did not alter V, rho or c, so the limit keeps the original arbitrary cover fixed.

Every countable delta-cover V of F was arbitrary in this argument. F004 bounds c by each of its (s+1)-costs, so taking their infimum gives H^s_delta(E)<=H^(s+1)_delta(F). The positive exponent s and scale delta were arbitrary. This proves the content inequality on their full stated domains, including n=0 and without any measurability assumption on cover members or their projections.

Assume L1: D>0. N002 gives D finite. Fix any 0<s<D. N001 gives H^s(E)=infinity. By definition H^s(E)=sup_{delta>0} H^s_delta(E); contents increase when the scale decreases, because fewer covers are admissible. Thus the left contents become arbitrarily large as delta decreases to zero: for any finite threshold choose one scale exceeding it, and all smaller scales also exceed it. N005 gives H^s_delta(E)<=H^(s+1)_delta(F) at each scale. Taking the supremum over scales therefore gives H^(s+1)(F)=infinity. Since s+1>0, N001 gives dim_H(F)>=s+1.

Use F001 for s increasing to D from below, possible because 0<D<infinity by N002 (for example s=D*(1-1/k) for integers k>=2). Then s+1 increases to D+1. The inequalities dim_H(F)>=s+1 imply dim_H(F)>=D+1, also if dim_H(F) is infinite. Discharge L1 and retain exactly the implication D>0 -> dim_H(F)>=D+1.

Assume L1: D=0. Nonemptiness H001 supplies a point of E. We will compare the copy of I above that point directly by covers, which proves the required instance of dimension monotonicity and isometry invariance without importing a further dimension theorem.

Choose x0 in E by H001 and define j:I->F by j(t)=(x0,t). Euclidean distance satisfies dist(j(t),j(u))=|t-u|, so j is an isometric embedding, including when n=0. For an arbitrary positive scale delta and any countable delta-cover V of F, its preimages {t in I:j(t) in V_i} cover I and have diameters no larger than diam(V_i), by the displayed distance equality. Thus H^s_delta(I)<=H^s_delta(F) for every s>0 and delta>0. Taking supremums over scales gives H^s(I)<=H^s(F). In particular for 0<s<1, N003 gives H^s(I)=infinity, so H^s(F)=infinity.

By N001 and F001, dim_H(F)>=s for every 0<s<1, so letting s increase to 1 gives dim_H(F)>=1. Under L1, 1=D+1. The construction used only a point x0 of E and the Euclidean product distance, so it includes n=0. Discharge L1 to obtain the claimed conditional lower bound.

N002 gives 0<=D<=n, hence D is a finite nonnegative real. Its exhaustive alternatives are D>0 or D=0. In the first alternative N006 yields dim_H(F)>=D+1; in the second N007 yields the same bound. N004 supplies dim_H(F)<=D+1 in both cases. Antisymmetry gives dim_H(F)=D+1. Substitute F=E x I, I=[0,1], D=dim_H(E) and the Euclidean coordinate identification from D001. This is dim_H(E x [0,1])=dim_H(E)+1 for the complete original nonnegative integer ambient range, including n=0.

1: import Mathlib
2: open scoped ENNReal NNReal
3: noncomputable section
4: abbrev YEucl (m : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)
5: def YI : Set ℝ := Set.Icc 0 1
6: def YJoin {m : ℕ} (x : YEucl m) (t : ℝ) : YEucl (m + 1) :=
7:   WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.snoc (fun i => x i) t)
8: def YBase {m : ℕ} (z : YEucl (m + 1)) : YEucl m :=
9:   WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => z i.castSucc)
10: def YLast {m : ℕ} (z : YEucl (m + 1)) : ℝ := z (Fin.last m)
11: def YF {m : ℕ} (A : Set (YEucl m)) : Set (YEucl (m + 1)) :=
12:   {z | ∃ x ∈ A, ∃ t ∈ YI, z = YJoin x t}
13: def YLine (t : ℝ) : YEucl 1 := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun _ => t)
14: def YCover {X : Type*} [PseudoEMetricSpace X]
15:     (δ : ℝ) (A : Set X) (U : ℕ → Set X) : Prop :=
16:   A ⊆ ⋃ i, U i ∧ ∀ i, Metric.ediam (U i) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal δ
17: def YCost {X : Type*} [PseudoEMetricSpace X]
18:     (s : ℝ) (U : ℕ → Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
19:   ∑' i, (Metric.ediam (U i)) ^ s
20: def YContent {X : Type*} [PseudoEMetricSpace X]
21:     (s δ : ℝ) (A : Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
22:   ⨅ (U : ℕ → Set X) (_ : YCover δ A U), YCost s U
23: def YHaus {X : Type*} [PseudoEMetricSpace X]
24:     (s : ℝ) (A : Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
25:   ⨆ (δ : ℝ) (_ : 0 < δ), YContent s δ A
26: def YCritical {X : Type*} [EMetricSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X]
27:     (A : Set X) : Prop :=
28:   0 ≤ dimH A ∧ ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s →
29:     YHaus s A = MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure s A ∧
30:     (dimH A < ENNReal.ofReal s → YHaus s A = 0) ∧
31:     (ENNReal.ofReal s < dimH A → YHaus s A = ⊤) ∧
32:     (YHaus s A = 0 → dimH A ≤ ENNReal.ofReal s) ∧
33:     (YHaus s A = ⊤ → ENNReal.ofReal s ≤ dimH A)

36: set_option autoImplicit false

38: #check (∀ (n : ℕ) (E : Set (YEucl n)) , ∀ (m : ℕ) (A : Set (YEucl m)) (s : ℝ), 0 < s → YHaus s A = MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure s A)
39: #check (∀ (n : ℕ) (E : Set (YEucl n)) (h_T001 : ∀ (m : ℕ) (A : Set (YEucl m)) (s : ℝ), 0 < s → YHaus s A = MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure s A), ∀ (m : ℕ) (A : Set (YEucl m)), YCritical A)
40: #check (∀ (n : ℕ) (E : Set (YEucl n)) (h_H002 : IsCompact E), (∃ L : ℝ, 0 < L ∧ ∀ x ∈ E, ∀ i : Fin n, |x i| ≤ L) ∧ (∀ (s δ : ℝ), 0 < s → 0 < δ → YContent s δ E < ⊤))
41: #check (∀ (n : ℕ) (E : Set (YEucl n)) (h_H001 : E.Nonempty) (h_T002 : ∀ (m : ℕ) (A : Set (YEucl m)), YCritical A) (h_T005 : (∃ L : ℝ, 0 < L ∧ ∀ x ∈ E, ∀ i : Fin n, |x i| ≤ L) ∧ (∀ (s δ : ℝ), 0 < s → 0 < δ → YContent s δ E < ⊤)), (0 ≤ dimH E ∧ dimH E ≤ (n : ℝ≥0∞) ∧ dimH E < ⊤) ∧ (n = 0 → E = Set.univ ∧ E.Subsingleton ∧ dimH E = 0) ∧ (∀ (s δ : ℝ), 0 < s → 0 < δ → YContent s δ E < ⊤))
42: #check (∀ (n : ℕ) (E : Set (YEucl n)) , (∀ (m : ℕ) (x y : YEucl m) (t u : ℝ), dist (YJoin x t) (YJoin y u) = Real.sqrt (dist x y ^ 2 + |t-u| ^ 2)) ∧ (∀ (m : ℕ) (z : YEucl (m+1)), YJoin (YBase z) (YLast z) = z) ∧ (∀ (m : ℕ) (x : YEucl m) (t : ℝ), YBase (YJoin x t) = x ∧ YLast (YJoin x t) = t) ∧ (∀ m : ℕ, LipschitzWith 1 (@YBase m) ∧ LipschitzWith 1 (@YLast m)) ∧ Isometry YLine ∧ Function.Surjective YLine)

value.text: Fix m,A and s>0 (L1). Apply M002 to Eucl(m), with its Euclidean extended metric and Borel measurable structure, exponent s and set A. At each finite positive scale its inner infimum is exactly H^s_delta(A): every countable cover is enumerable by naturals, with empty padding if needed, and each nonempty-member inner supremum is just its diameter to power s, whereas an empty member has cost zero. At a finite scale all nonempty admissible diameters are finite, so ediam and the usual diameter agree. The additional native scale infinity does not change the outer supremum: its admissible covers include those at every finite scale, so its infimum is no larger. Every positive finite extended scale is a positive real scale. Thus M002 gives muH[s](A)=sup_delta H^s_delta(A)=H^s(A).

Use F001. The native dimension dimH(A) is dim_H(A) by the representation in D006 and is nonnegative because it is a supremum in [0,infinity]. Regard s as a nonnegative real, using s>0. M003 gives infinity when s<dim_H(A); M004 gives zero when dim_H(A)<s. If H^s(A)=0, F001 makes the native measure zero and hence unequal to infinity, so M005 gives dim_H(A)<=s. If H^s(A)=infinity, F001 and M006 give s<=dim_H(A). These conclusions hold for the arbitrary Euclidean dimension m and set A, including infinite dimension values. Discharge L1 and universally quantify: all the asserted clauses follow.

H002 gives compactness. The open balls of radius delta/2 centered at points of E form an open cover; a finite subcover has diameters at most delta and finite s-cost. Thus H^s_delta(E) is finite for arbitrary s>0,delta>0. Also the increasing boxes (-k,k)^n, for positive integer k, cover Eucl(n). A finite subcover of E places E in some [-L,L]^n with L>0. This proves the required existence of a bounding box. Nonnegativity of D follows from N001.

For the branch L1: n>=1, choose the bounding box from F001. Subdivide each coordinate interval [-L,L] into ceil(2L/h) pieces of length at most h, where 0<h<=1. Taking products covers the box by at most (2L/h+1)^n <= C h^(-n) cubes, where C=(2L+2)^n. Each cube has Euclidean diameter at most sqrt(n) h. Hence for any a>n the total a-cost is at most C n^(a/2) h^(a-n), tending to zero as h decreases to zero; the maximum diameter tends to zero as well. For each fixed positive scale these covers eventually satisfy its diameter bound and have arbitrarily small cost. Thus H^a(E)=0. N001 gives D<=a for all a>n, hence D<=n (otherwise choose a strictly between n and D; if D=infinity any a>n contradicts D<=a). Discharge L1 to obtain the conditional branch conclusion.

For the branch L2: n=0, H001 and the fact that Eucl(0) has just its empty tuple give E=Eucl(0), a singleton. For every positive exponent its one-member singleton cover has diameter and cost zero at every scale. N001 therefore gives D is at most every positive real exponent; together with nonnegativity this is D=0. Discharge L2. Since a natural n is either zero or at least one, F003 and this branch yield 0<=D<=n, with the stated singleton assertion when n=0. F002 supplies the finite-content clause.

For any a>1 and each positive integer k, the k closed intervals [j/k,(j+1)/k], 0<=j<k, cover I. Their diameters are 1/k, and their total a-cost is k*(1/k)^a=k^(1-a), tending to zero as k tends to infinity. At any fixed scale the diameter bound holds for all sufficiently large k. Hence the a-content of I is zero at every positive scale and H^a(I)=0 for every a>1.

Fix delta>0 and an arbitrary countable delta-cover T of I. Ignore empty terms by K={i:T_i nonempty}, and set rho_i=diam(T_i)<=delta. For epsilon>0 the bounded nonempty real set T_i has infimum and supremum, with sup T_i-inf T_i=rho_i. Define the open interval J_i=(inf T_i-epsilon*2^(-i-2),sup T_i+epsilon*2^(-i-2)); it contains T_i and has length rho_i+epsilon*2^(-i-1). These intervals cover I. Countable subadditivity of Lebesgue length, lambda(I)=1, and the geometric sum over K bounded by the full sum over N give 1<=sum_i lambda(J_i)<=sum_i rho_i+epsilon. If sum_i rho_i is infinite the claim is immediate; otherwise letting epsilon decrease to zero gives sum_i rho_i>=1. This holds for the arbitrary cover and scale.

For arbitrary 0<s<1, retain delta and T, K, rho. For 0<rho_i<=delta the negative exponent s-1 gives rho_i^(s-1)>=delta^(s-1), hence rho_i^s>=delta^(s-1)*rho_i. When rho_i=0 the same inequality is 0>=0, since s>0. Sum the inequalities and apply F002: sum_i rho_i^s>=delta^(s-1)*sum_i rho_i>=delta^(s-1). The same holds with empty terms contributing zero. Take the infimum over the arbitrary delta-covers to obtain H^s_delta(I)>=delta^(s-1). Since s-1<0 this lower bound tends to infinity as delta decreases to zero; consequently H^s(I)=infinity for every 0<s<1. This also records the coverwise bound required in the output.

Apply N001 with m=1 on the real Euclidean line: identify a real number with its one-coordinate vector in Eucl(1), preserving distance by the Euclidean formula. F001 gives dim_H(I)<=a for every a>1, hence dim_H(I)<=1. F003 gives dim_H(I)>=s for every 0<s<1, hence dim_H(I)>=1 by real order completeness. Together these yield dim_H(I)=1, and F001,F002,F003 retain all of the additional estimates asserted in the output.

First treat L1: n=0. N002 gives E=Eucl(0), a singleton, and D=0. The map from I to F sending t to the concatenated point ((),t) is onto and preserves all distances by the Euclidean formula. N003 gives H^a(I)=0 for every a>1. For any positive scale and cost tolerance, choose a cover of I at that scale with cost below the tolerance, intersect each cover member with I, and send it through this map. These sets cover F and have no larger diameters or costs. Thus H^a(F)=0 for every a>1. By N001, dim_H(F)<=a for every a>1, hence dim_H(F)<=1=D+1. Discharge L1 and retain this branch conclusion.

Assume L2: n>=1. Fix q>D. N002 implies q>0, and N001 gives H^q(E)=0. Thus for any 0<r<=1 and epsilon>0 the infimum H^q_r(E)=0 supplies a countable r-cover with cost below epsilon/2. Discard its empty members. Each remaining zero-diameter set is a singleton. Enumerate such members by their original natural indices i and replace the i-th by a ball centered at that singleton, of positive diameter at most r and with q-cost <epsilon*2^(-i-2). Such balls exist in Eucl(n) because n>=1: their diameters are twice their positive radii, which may be made arbitrarily small since q>0. The replacement costs sum to at most epsilon/2 (indeed the strict bounds have that geometric majorant); with the initial strict epsilon/2 bound the final cost is <epsilon. Unchanged positive-diameter members already have diameter <=r. This proves existence of the positive-diameter cover needed next.

Choose U as in F002 and put r_i=diam(U_i), N_i=ceil(1/r_i). The N_i intervals [j/N_i,(j+1)/N_i], 0<=j<N_i, cover I and have length 1/N_i<=r_i. Since r_i<=1, N_i<=1/r_i+1<=2/r_i. The products of U_i with these intervals form a countable cover of F: a countable union of finite families is countable. By the Euclidean product distance, each product diameter is at most sqrt(2)*r_i. Thus their total (q+1)-cost is at most sum_i N_i*(sqrt(2)*r_i)^(q+1) <= 2*(sqrt(2))^(q+1)*sum_i r_i^q < 2*(sqrt(2))^(q+1)*epsilon. Since r and epsilon were arbitrary and the remaining branch assumption concerns only n, universally quantify them in this cover-existence conclusion.

For an arbitrary target scale delta>0, apply the universally quantified construction F003 with its scale parameter equal to min(1,delta/sqrt(2)), which is strictly positive, and with arbitrary positive cost parameter. The resulting covers are delta-covers of F. Let that cost parameter decrease to zero; the multiplier 2*(sqrt(2))^(q+1) is fixed and finite, so H^(q+1)_delta(F)=0. The scale delta was arbitrary, hence H^(q+1)(F)=0. By N001, dim_H(F)<=q+1. Since q>D was arbitrary, universally quantify q in this conclusion.

N002 makes D finite. Since q>D was arbitrary, F004 holds for every such q. Let q decrease to D (equivalently use q=D+1/k for positive integers k); this gives dim_H(F)<=D+1. Discharge L2. Together with F001 and the exhaustive alternatives n=0 or n>=1, this proves the upper bound.

Fix s>0 and delta>0 and put c=H^s_delta(E). N002 proves c finite. Take an arbitrary countable delta-cover V of F, and restrict to its nonempty-member indices K, a subset of N. Put rho_i=diam(V_i), A_i=the first-coordinate projection of V_i, and B_i=the last-coordinate projection. By the Euclidean distance formula each coordinate projection is 1-Lipschitz: dist of projected points is no more than dist of the original points. Consequently diam(A_i)<=rho_i and diam(B_i)<=rho_i<=delta. Every B_i is nonempty and bounded; its infimum and supremum are finite and sup B_i-inf B_i<=rho_i. No measurability of V_i,A_i or B_i is asserted or needed.

For epsilon>0 define eta_i=epsilon*2^(-i-1)/(1+rho_i^s)>0 and J_i=(inf B_i-eta_i/2,sup B_i+eta_i/2). F001 makes these finite open intervals containing B_i, with length at most rho_i+eta_i. Define f_i(t)=rho_i^s*1_{J_i}(t). Each coefficient is finite and nonnegative, each J_i is open, and therefore every f_i is Lebesgue measurable, hence almost everywhere measurable for lambda restricted to I. The family has countable index set K.

For each t in I the A_i with t in J_i cover E: given x in E, the point (x,t) belongs to F and hence to some V_i. That index lies in K, x belongs to A_i, and t belongs to B_i subset J_i by F002. These A_i have diameter <=rho_i<=delta by F001, so they are an admissible countable delta-cover of E. Its s-cost is at most sum_i rho_i^s*1_{J_i}(t)=sum_i f_i(t). The definition of c as an infimum gives c<=sum_i f_i(t) for every t in I.

Integrate F003 against lambda restricted to I. Since lambda(I)=1, the integral of the finite constant c is c. Apply M001 with X=R, K the countable subset of N above, mu=lambda restricted to I, and the nonnegative measurable family f from F002. It gives integral_I sum_i f_i = sum_i integral_I f_i. For each i, integration of its indicator times the constant gives integral_I f_i=rho_i^s*lambda(J_i intersect I). Thus, using F002,
c <= sum_i rho_i^s*lambda(J_i intersect I) <= sum_i rho_i^s*(rho_i+eta_i) = sum_i rho_i^(s+1)+sum_i eta_i*rho_i^s <= sum_i rho_i^(s+1)+epsilon.
The last bound follows termwise from eta_i*rho_i^s=epsilon*2^(-i-1)*rho_i^s/(1+rho_i^s)<=epsilon*2^(-i-1) and sum_{i in K}2^(-i-1)<=1. All inequalities are valid for nonnegative extended sums. If the cost sum_i rho_i^(s+1) is infinite, c<=that cost immediately. Otherwise the cost and c are finite, and since this estimate is available for every epsilon>0, let epsilon decrease to zero to obtain c<=sum_i rho_i^(s+1). The interval enlargement did not alter V, rho or c, so the limit keeps the original arbitrary cover fixed.

Every countable delta-cover V of F was arbitrary in this argument. F004 bounds c by each of its (s+1)-costs, so taking their infimum gives H^s_delta(E)<=H^(s+1)_delta(F). The positive exponent s and scale delta were arbitrary. This proves the content inequality on their full stated domains, including n=0 and without any measurability assumption on cover members or their projections.

Assume L1: D>0. N002 gives D finite. Fix any 0<s<D. N001 gives H^s(E)=infinity. By definition H^s(E)=sup_{delta>0} H^s_delta(E); contents increase when the scale decreases, because fewer covers are admissible. Thus the left contents become arbitrarily large as delta decreases to zero: for any finite threshold choose one scale exceeding it, and all smaller scales also exceed it. N005 gives H^s_delta(E)<=H^(s+1)_delta(F) at each scale. Taking the supremum over scales therefore gives H^(s+1)(F)=infinity. Since s+1>0, N001 gives dim_H(F)>=s+1.

Use F001 for s increasing to D from below, possible because 0<D<infinity by N002 (for example s=D*(1-1/k) for integers k>=2). Then s+1 increases to D+1. The inequalities dim_H(F)>=s+1 imply dim_H(F)>=D+1, also if dim_H(F) is infinite. Discharge L1 and retain exactly the implication D>0 -> dim_H(F)>=D+1.

Assume L1: D=0. Nonemptiness H001 supplies a point of E. We will compare the copy of I above that point directly by covers, which proves the required instance of dimension monotonicity and isometry invariance without importing a further dimension theorem.

Choose x0 in E by H001 and define j:I->F by j(t)=(x0,t). Euclidean distance satisfies dist(j(t),j(u))=|t-u|, so j is an isometric embedding, including when n=0. For an arbitrary positive scale delta and any countable delta-cover V of F, its preimages {t in I:j(t) in V_i} cover I and have diameters no larger than diam(V_i), by the displayed distance equality. Thus H^s_delta(I)<=H^s_delta(F) for every s>0 and delta>0. Taking supremums over scales gives H^s(I)<=H^s(F). In particular for 0<s<1, N003 gives H^s(I)=infinity, so H^s(F)=infinity.

By N001 and F001, dim_H(F)>=s for every 0<s<1, so letting s increase to 1 gives dim_H(F)>=1. Under L1, 1=D+1. The construction used only a point x0 of E and the Euclidean product distance, so it includes n=0. Discharge L1 to obtain the claimed conditional lower bound.

N002 gives 0<=D<=n, hence D is a finite nonnegative real. Its exhaustive alternatives are D>0 or D=0. In the first alternative N006 yields dim_H(F)>=D+1; in the second N007 yields the same bound. N004 supplies dim_H(F)<=D+1 in both cases. Antisymmetry gives dim_H(F)=D+1. Substitute F=E x I, I=[0,1], D=dim_H(E) and the Euclidean coordinate identification from D001. This is dim_H(E x [0,1])=dim_H(E)+1 for the complete original nonnegative integer ambient range, including n=0.

locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary natural number m.
Fix an arbitrary subset A of Eucl(m).
Fix an arbitrary real s, and assume L1: s>0.

argument.text: Fix m,A and s>0 (L1). Apply M002 to Eucl(m), with its Euclidean extended metric and Borel measurable structure, exponent s and set A. At each finite positive scale its inner infimum is exactly H^s_delta(A): every countable cover is enumerable by naturals, with empty padding if needed, and each nonempty-member inner supremum is just its diameter to power s, whereas an empty member has cost zero. At a finite scale all nonempty admissible diameters are finite, so ediam and the usual diameter agree. The additional native scale infinity does not change the outer supremum: its admissible covers include those at every finite scale, so its infimum is no larger. Every positive finite extended scale is a positive real scale. Thus M002 gives muH[s](A)=sup_delta H^s_delta(A)=H^s(A).

Use F001. The native dimension dimH(A) is dim_H(A) by the representation in D006 and is nonnegative because it is a supremum in [0,infinity]. Regard s as a nonnegative real, using s>0. M003 gives infinity when s<dim_H(A); M004 gives zero when dim_H(A)<s. If H^s(A)=0, F001 makes the native measure zero and hence unequal to infinity, so M005 gives dim_H(A)<=s. If H^s(A)=infinity, F001 and M006 give s<=dim_H(A). These conclusions hold for the arbitrary Euclidean dimension m and set A, including infinite dimension values. Discharge L1 and universally quantify: all the asserted clauses follow.

hypothesis_checks: Eucl(m) has its Euclidean metric, hence an extended metric.
The chosen measurable structure is Borel by construction.

applications.bindings: X=Eucl(m), source set=A, source nonnegative exponent a=s; apply in the conditional subcase s<dim_H(A).
hypothesis_checks: Eucl(m) is a Euclidean metric space.
Use its Borel measurable structure.
L1 gives s>0, hence s>=0.
The antecedent s<dim_H(A)=dimH(A) is precisely the condition of the asserted implication.

hypothesis_checks: Eucl(m) is a Euclidean metric space.
Use its Borel measurable structure.

The antecedent dim_H(A)<s is dimH(A)<s by D006.

hypothesis_checks: Eucl(m) has its Euclidean metric.

locals.declaration: For the finite-content assertion, take arbitrary s>0.
Take an arbitrary scale delta>0.
Choose L>0 with E contained in [-L,L]^n, whose existence is F001.
Define C=(2L+2)^n.
Let 0<h<=1 vary towards zero.
Fix an arbitrary exponent a>n.

argument.text: H002 gives compactness. The open balls of radius delta/2 centered at points of E form an open cover; a finite subcover has diameters at most delta and finite s-cost. Thus H^s_delta(E) is finite for arbitrary s>0,delta>0. Also the increasing boxes (-k,k)^n, for positive integer k, cover Eucl(n). A finite subcover of E places E in some [-L,L]^n with L>0. This proves the required existence of a bounding box. Nonnegativity of D follows from N001.

produces.statement: There exists a real L_b>0 such that E is contained in [-L_b,L_b]^n.
For every s_b>0 and delta_b>0, H^{s_b}_{delta_b}(E)<infinity.

argument.text: For the branch L1: n>=1, choose the bounding box from F001. Subdivide each coordinate interval [-L,L] into ceil(2L/h) pieces of length at most h, where 0<h<=1. Taking products covers the box by at most (2L/h+1)^n <= C h^(-n) cubes, where C=(2L+2)^n. Each cube has Euclidean diameter at most sqrt(n) h. Hence for any a>n the total a-cost is at most C n^(a/2) h^(a-n), tending to zero as h decreases to zero; the maximum diameter tends to zero as well. For each fixed positive scale these covers eventually satisfy its diameter bound and have arbitrarily small cost. Thus H^a(E)=0. N001 gives D<=a for all a>n, hence D<=n (otherwise choose a strictly between n and D; if D=infinity any a>n contradicts D<=a). Discharge L1 to obtain the conditional branch conclusion.

For the branch L2: n=0, H001 and the fact that Eucl(0) has just its empty tuple give E=Eucl(0), a singleton. For every positive exponent its one-member singleton cover has diameter and cost zero at every scale. N001 therefore gives D is at most every positive real exponent; together with nonnegativity this is D=0. Discharge L2. Since a natural n is either zero or at least one, F003 and this branch yield 0<=D<=n, with the stated singleton assertion when n=0. F002 supplies the finite-content clause.

Fix a positive real scale delta.

argument.text: For any a>1 and each positive integer k, the k closed intervals [j/k,(j+1)/k], 0<=j<k, cover I. Their diameters are 1/k, and their total a-cost is k*(1/k)^a=k^(1-a), tending to zero as k tends to infinity. At any fixed scale the diameter bound holds for all sufficiently large k. Hence the a-content of I is zero at every positive scale and H^a(I)=0 for every a>1.

Fix delta>0 and an arbitrary countable delta-cover T of I. Ignore empty terms by K={i:T_i nonempty}, and set rho_i=diam(T_i)<=delta. For epsilon>0 the bounded nonempty real set T_i has infimum and supremum, with sup T_i-inf T_i=rho_i. Define the open interval J_i=(inf T_i-epsilon*2^(-i-2),sup T_i+epsilon*2^(-i-2)); it contains T_i and has length rho_i+epsilon*2^(-i-1). These intervals cover I. Countable subadditivity of Lebesgue length, lambda(I)=1, and the geometric sum over K bounded by the full sum over N give 1<=sum_i lambda(J_i)<=sum_i rho_i+epsilon. If sum_i rho_i is infinite the claim is immediate; otherwise letting epsilon decrease to zero gives sum_i rho_i>=1. This holds for the arbitrary cover and scale.

produces.statement: For every positive scale delta_b and every countable delta_b-cover T_b of I, the sum of its nonempty-member diameters is at least 1.

argument.text: For arbitrary 0<s<1, retain delta and T, K, rho. For 0<rho_i<=delta the negative exponent s-1 gives rho_i^(s-1)>=delta^(s-1), hence rho_i^s>=delta^(s-1)*rho_i. When rho_i=0 the same inequality is 0>=0, since s>0. Sum the inequalities and apply F002: sum_i rho_i^s>=delta^(s-1)*sum_i rho_i>=delta^(s-1). The same holds with empty terms contributing zero. Take the infimum over the arbitrary delta-covers to obtain H^s_delta(I)>=delta^(s-1). Since s-1<0 this lower bound tends to infinity as delta decreases to zero; consequently H^s(I)=infinity for every 0<s<1. This also records the coverwise bound required in the output.

produces.statement: For every 0<s_b<1, H^{s_b}(I)=infinity; for every delta_b>0 every countable delta_b-cover of I with diameter sequence rho_b satisfies sum_i rho_b(i)^{s_b}>=delta_b^(s_b-1).

argument.text: Apply N001 with m=1 on the real Euclidean line: identify a real number with its one-coordinate vector in Eucl(1), preserving distance by the Euclidean formula. F001 gives dim_H(I)<=a for every a>1, hence dim_H(I)<=1. F003 gives dim_H(I)>=s for every 0<s<1, hence dim_H(I)>=1 by real order completeness. Together these yield dim_H(I)=1, and F001,F002,F003 retain all of the additional estimates asserted in the output.

Fix 0<r<=1.
Fix epsilon>0.

locals.declaration: Choose a cover U of E with all member diameters r_i strictly positive and <=r, and sum_i r_i^q<epsilon, as established in F002.
