argument.text: First treat L1: n=0. N002 gives E=Eucl(0), a singleton, and D=0. The map from I to F sending t to the concatenated point ((),t) is onto and preserves all distances by the Euclidean formula. N003 gives H^a(I)=0 for every a>1. For any positive scale and cost tolerance, choose a cover of I at that scale with cost below the tolerance, intersect each cover member with I, and send it through this map. These sets cover F and have no larger diameters or costs. Thus H^a(F)=0 for every a>1. By N001, dim_H(F)<=a for every a>1, hence dim_H(F)<=1=D+1. Discharge L1 and retain this branch conclusion.

Assume L2: n>=1. Fix q>D. N002 implies q>0, and N001 gives H^q(E)=0. Thus for any 0<r<=1 and epsilon>0 the infimum H^q_r(E)=0 supplies a countable r-cover with cost below epsilon/2. Discard its empty members. Each remaining zero-diameter set is a singleton. Enumerate such members by their original natural indices i and replace the i-th by a ball centered at that singleton, of positive diameter at most r and with q-cost <epsilon*2^(-i-2). Such balls exist in Eucl(n) because n>=1: their diameters are twice their positive radii, which may be made arbitrarily small since q>0. The replacement costs sum to at most epsilon/2 (indeed the strict bounds have that geometric majorant); with the initial strict epsilon/2 bound the final cost is <epsilon. Unchanged positive-diameter members already have diameter <=r. This proves existence of the positive-diameter cover needed next.

binders.type: countable family of subsets of Eucl(n)

argument.text: Choose U as in F002 and put r_i=diam(U_i), N_i=ceil(1/r_i). The N_i intervals [j/N_i,(j+1)/N_i], 0<=j<N_i, cover I and have length 1/N_i<=r_i. Since r_i<=1, N_i<=1/r_i+1<=2/r_i. The products of U_i with these intervals form a countable cover of F: a countable union of finite families is countable. By the Euclidean product distance, each product diameter is at most sqrt(2)*r_i. Thus their total (q+1)-cost is at most sum_i N_i*(sqrt(2)*r_i)^(q+1) <= 2*(sqrt(2))^(q+1)*sum_i r_i^q < 2*(sqrt(2))^(q+1)*epsilon. Since r and epsilon were arbitrary and the remaining branch assumption concerns only n, universally quantify them in this cover-existence conclusion.

produces.statement: Under n>=1, for every scale r_b with 0<r_b<=1 and every epsilon_b>0 there is a countable cover of F with all diameters at most sqrt(2)*r_b and total (q+1)-cost less than 2*(sqrt(2))^(q+1)*epsilon_b.

argument.text: For an arbitrary target scale delta>0, apply the universally quantified construction F003 with its scale parameter equal to min(1,delta/sqrt(2)), which is strictly positive, and with arbitrary positive cost parameter. The resulting covers are delta-covers of F. Let that cost parameter decrease to zero; the multiplier 2*(sqrt(2))^(q+1) is fixed and finite, so H^(q+1)_delta(F)=0. The scale delta was arbitrary, hence H^(q+1)(F)=0. By N001, dim_H(F)<=q+1. Since q>D was arbitrary, universally quantify q in this conclusion.

produces.statement: Under n>=1, for every real q_b>D, H^(q_b+1)(F)=0 and dim_H(F)<=q_b+1.

argument.text: N002 makes D finite. Since q>D was arbitrary, F004 holds for every such q. Let q decrease to D (equivalently use q=D+1/k for positive integers k); this gives dim_H(F)<=D+1. Discharge L2. Together with F001 and the exhaustive alternatives n=0 or n>=1, this proves the upper bound.

241: /-- A finite, mutually orthogonal family of subspaces of `E`, which span `E`, induce an isometry
242: from `E` to `PiLp 2` of the subspaces equipped with the `L2` inner product. -/
243: def DirectSum.IsInternal.isometryL2OfOrthogonalFamily [DecidableEq ι] {V : ι → Submodule 𝕜 E}
244:     (hV : DirectSum.IsInternal V)
245:     (hV' : OrthogonalFamily 𝕜 (fun i => V i) fun i => (V i).subtypeₗᵢ) :
246:     E ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] PiLp 2 fun i => V i := by
247:   let e₁ := DirectSum.linearEquivFunOnFintype 𝕜 ι fun i => V i
248:   let e₂ := LinearEquiv.ofBijective (DirectSum.coeLinearMap V) hV
249:   refine LinearEquiv.isometryOfInner ((e₂.symm.trans e₁).trans
250:     (WithLp.linearEquiv 2 𝕜 (Π i, V i)).symm) ?_
251:   suffices ∀ (v w : PiLp 2 fun i => V i), ⟪v, w⟫ = ⟪e₂ (e₁.symm v), e₂ (e₁.symm w)⟫ by
252:     intro v₀ w₀
253:     simp only [LinearEquiv.trans_apply]
254:     convert! this (toLp 2 (e₁ (e₂.symm v₀))) (toLp 2 (e₁ (e₂.symm w₀))) <;> simp
255:   intro v w
256:   trans ⟪∑ i, (V i).subtypeₗᵢ (v i), ∑ i, (V i).subtypeₗᵢ (w i)⟫
257:   · simp only [sum_inner, hV'.inner_right_fintype, PiLp.inner_apply]
258:   · congr <;> simp
259: 
260: set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
261: @[simp]
262: theorem DirectSum.IsInternal.isometryL2OfOrthogonalFamily_symm_apply [DecidableEq ι]
263:     {V : ι → Submodule 𝕜 E} (hV : DirectSum.IsInternal V)
264:     (hV' : OrthogonalFamily 𝕜 (fun i => V i) fun i => (V i).subtypeₗᵢ) (w : PiLp 2 fun i => V i) :
265:     (hV.isometryL2OfOrthogonalFamily hV').symm w = ∑ i, (w i : E) := by
266:   classical
267:     let e₁ := DirectSum.linearEquivFunOnFintype 𝕜 ι fun i => V i
268:     let e₂ := LinearEquiv.ofBijective (DirectSum.coeLinearMap V) hV
269:     suffices ∀ v : ⨁ i, V i, e₂ v = ∑ i, e₁ v i by exact this (e₁.symm w)

argument.text: Fix s>0 and delta>0 and put c=H^s_delta(E). N002 proves c finite. Take an arbitrary countable delta-cover V of F, and restrict to its nonempty-member indices K, a subset of N. Put rho_i=diam(V_i), A_i=the first-coordinate projection of V_i, and B_i=the last-coordinate projection. By the Euclidean distance formula each coordinate projection is 1-Lipschitz: dist of projected points is no more than dist of the original points. Consequently diam(A_i)<=rho_i and diam(B_i)<=rho_i<=delta. Every B_i is nonempty and bounded; its infimum and supremum are finite and sup B_i-inf B_i<=rho_i. No measurability of V_i,A_i or B_i is asserted or needed.

produces.statement: c<infinity; for every i in K, A_i and B_i are nonempty, diam(A_i)<=rho_i, 0<=rho_i<=delta, B_i is bounded in R, and sup B_i-inf B_i<=rho_i.

argument.text: For epsilon>0 define eta_i=epsilon*2^(-i-1)/(1+rho_i^s)>0 and J_i=(inf B_i-eta_i/2,sup B_i+eta_i/2). F001 makes these finite open intervals containing B_i, with length at most rho_i+eta_i. Define f_i(t)=rho_i^s*1_{J_i}(t). Each coefficient is finite and nonnegative, each J_i is open, and therefore every f_i is Lebesgue measurable, hence almost everywhere measurable for lambda restricted to I. The family has countable index set K.

produces.statement: For every i in K, B_i is contained in J_i, J_i is an open bounded interval with lambda(J_i)<=rho_i+eta_i, and f_i is nonnegative and measurable for lambda restricted to I. The set K is countable.

argument.text: For each t in I the A_i with t in J_i cover E: given x in E, the point (x,t) belongs to F and hence to some V_i. That index lies in K, x belongs to A_i, and t belongs to B_i subset J_i by F002. These A_i have diameter <=rho_i<=delta by F001, so they are an admissible countable delta-cover of E. Its s-cost is at most sum_i rho_i^s*1_{J_i}(t)=sum_i f_i(t). The definition of c as an infimum gives c<=sum_i f_i(t) for every t in I.

argument.text:
Integrate F003 against lambda restricted to I. Since lambda(I)=1, the integral of the finite constant c is c. Apply M001 with X=R, K the countable subset of N above, mu=lambda restricted to I, and the nonnegative measurable family f from F002. It gives integral_I sum_i f_i = sum_i integral_I f_i. For each i, integration of its indicator times the constant gives integral_I f_i=rho_i^s*lambda(J_i intersect I). Thus, using F002,

argument.text: Assume L1: D>0. N002 gives D finite. Fix any 0<s<D. N001 gives H^s(E)=infinity. By definition H^s(E)=sup_{delta>0} H^s_delta(E); contents increase when the scale decreases, because fewer covers are admissible. argument.text: Assume L1: D=0. Nonemptiness H001 supplies a point of E. We will compare the copy of I above that point directly by covers, which proves the required instance of dimension monotonicity and isometry invariance without importing a further dimension theorem.

Choose x0 in E by H001 and define j:I->F by j(t)=(x0,t). Euclidean distance satisfies dist(j(t),j(u))=|t-u|, so j is an isometric embedding, including when n=0. For an arbitrary positive scale delta and any countable delta-cover V of F, its preimages {t in I:j(t) in V_i} cover I and have diameters no larger than diam(V_i), by the displayed distance equality. Thus H^s_delta(I)<=H^s_delta(F) for every s>0 and delta>0. Taking supremums over scales gives H^s(I)<=H^s(F). In particular for 0<s<1, N003 gives H^s(I)=infinity, so H^s(F)=infinity.

N002 gives 0<=D<=n, hence D is a finite nonnegative real. Its exhaustive alternatives are D>0 or D=0. In the first alternative N006 yields dim_H(F)>=D+1; in the second N007 yields the same bound. N004 supplies dim_H(F)<=D+1 in both cases. Antisymmetry gives dim_H(F)=D+1. Substitute F=E x I, I=[0,1], D=dim_H(E) and the Euclidean coordinate identification from D001. This is dim_H(E x [0,1])=dim_H(E)+1 for the complete original nonnegative integer ambient range, including n=0.

25: ## Main definitions
26: 
27: * `WithLp p V`: a copy of `V` to be equipped with an L`p` norm.
28: * `WithLp.toLp`: the canonical inclusion from `V` to `WithLp p V`.
29: * `WithLp.ofLp`: the canonical inclusion from `WithLp p V` to `V`.
30: * `WithLp.linearEquiv p K V`: the canonical `K`-module isomorphism between `WithLp p V` and `V`.
31: 
32: ## Implementation notes
33: 
34: The pattern here is the same one as is used by `Lex` for order structures; it avoids having a
35: separate synonym for each type (`ProdLp`, `PiLp`, etc), and allows all the structure-copying code
36: to be shared.
37: 
38: TODO: is it safe to copy across the topology and uniform space structure too for all reasonable
39: choices of `V`?
40: -/
41:

47: /-- A type synonym for the given `V`, associated with the L`p` norm. Note that by default this just
48: forgets the norm structure on `V`; it is up to downstream users to implement the L`p` norm (for
49: instance, on `Prod` and finite `Pi` types). -/
50: structure WithLp (p : ℝ≥0∞) (V : Type*) where
51:   /-- Converts an element of `V` to an element of `WithLp p V`. -/
52:   toLp (p) ::
53:   /-- Converts an element of `WithLp p V` to an element of `V`. -/
54:   ofLp : V
